en.headline: Ocean Park’s Reptile Territory opens to public on Friday with nearly 20 species
en.dek: The new Summit pavilion features endangered rhinoceros iguanas, Chinese crocodile lizards and blue-tongued skinks, some rescued by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department.
body: Ocean Park on Wednesday held the opening ceremony for its first dedicated reptile pavilion, Reptile Territory, which will admit annual pass holders on Thursday and the general public from Friday.

The exhibit houses nearly 20 species from around the world, including the nationally first-class protected Chinese crocodile lizard, the endangered rhinoceros iguana, panther chameleons, blue-tongued skinks and sailfin lizards. Some of the animals were confiscated by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department during enforcement actions and later placed in the park’s care after rehabilitation.

Park chairman Paulo Pong said the display aims to reduce common misconceptions about reptiles and discourage the illegal wildlife trade. Daily programmes include animal talks and a “Reptile Press Conference” where visitors can observe feeding behaviour at close range. Interactive panels and an AI species-recognition app provide additional information on habitats and conservation.

zh.headline: 海洋公園爬行探索基地周五起對公眾開放 展出近20種爬行動物
zh.dek: 高峰樂園新展館包括國家一級保護瑤山鱷蜥、瀕危犀牛鬣蜥及藍舌石龍子等，部分動物來自漁護署充公後由園方護理。
body: 海洋公園周三為全新「爬行探索基地」舉行開幕禮，周四起優先開放予全年會員，周五起對公眾開放。
展館位於高峰樂園，匯集近20種來自世界各地的爬行動物，包括國家一級保護的瑤山鱷蜥、瀕危犀牛鬣蜥、七彩變色龍、藍舌石龍子及斑帆蜥等。部分動物由漁護署執法充公後交由園方照顧及康復。
海洋公園主席龐建貽表示，展館希望減少公眾對爬行動物的誤解，並提醒切勿因好奇購買不適合家居飼養的物種。每日設有動物趣談及「爬爬記者會」，讓訪客近距離觀察進食及護理；亦設互動展板及人工智能物種辨識應用程式提供生態資訊。
